evidenceBasis: Completed bounded official-source review of historical production, with consolidation resolutions; not actual older-cluster integration.
currentSourceApplicability: Requires reassessment after production layout changes.

findings.change: Production and fixture API versions remain served; GA API additions and unrelated removals do not require endpoint changes.
findings.assessment: The converter uses stable DC/apps/core/HPA v2/policy v1 APIs and optional discovered admin policies. It does not create admissionregistration v1beta1, APF versions, kubeadm output objects, CRDs or cloud-provider configurations. OpenShift 4.18 warns that 4.17 accidentally reintroduced admissionregistration v1beta1; that does not make it a converter dependency.

findings.change: AppArmor gains Pod/container fields in1.30, loses NodeReady indication, and changes kubelet soft rejection to hard admission in1.31.
findings.assessment: New appArmorProfile fields require manual review under the1.27 raw baseline. Upstream PR123435 pod PrepareForCreate/applyAppArmorVersionSkew copies valid beta runtime/default, localhost/<profile> and unconfined annotations to appArmorProfile when AppArmorFields is enabled; raw Pod dry-run validation therefore already catches this path. PR125776 moves the same kubelet handler from soft to hard admission: unsupported profiles already prevented startup before1.31. No newly successful-before/failing-after annotation value was established. Node-local support/profile availability is not proven by NodeReady or API acceptance.
requiredAction: Add a focused contract for a valid beta annotation defaulted into a post-baseline appArmorProfile and assert refusal before source/HPA mutation. Do not add a blanket new guard solely from the hard-versus-soft wording.
residualScope: Older or feature-disabled annotation-only paths require reviewed node/runtime profile availability; no real older AppArmor cluster was tested.

findings.change: User namespaces, recursive readonly mounts, native sidecars and newer placement/security fields change workload semantics.
findings.assessment: Post1.27 spec fields (appArmorProfile, recursiveReadOnly, native-sidecar restartPolicy, image volumes, supplementalGroupsPolicy and newer affinity fields) are retained only for review through raw validation and cannot silently round-trip. Existing baseline hostUsers/procMount/securityContext strings are preserved, with real Pod admission determining the enabled gate/SCC/PSA contract. Runtime support for user namespaces and SELinux is a cluster prerequisite; raw validation alone does not prove it. Required inter-Pod affinity, hard topology spread, dynamic claims, scheduling gates and custom schedulers already block automated placement.
residualScope: Admission is authoritative for same-cluster execution, not evidence that feature-gated input can run across every older cluster.

findings.change: Native-sidecar allocation, in-place resize and DRA quota changes require the correct resource interpretation.
findings.assessment: Existing podResources counts restartable init sidecars, peak non-sidecar initialization and overhead. observedPodRequests uses the larger spec/allocated/status requests. DRA destination claims already require manual review; post-baseline Pod budgets from admission are rejected. Unknown quota scopes/operators do not silently pass. Device health allocatedResourcesStatus is not a replacement quantity budget.
residualScope: Point-in-time quota/capacity checks reserve no resources and do not reproduce CPU/NUMA-manager or custom scheduler behavior.

findings.change: Per-container resource metrics become stable;1.31 removes long-nonfunctional controller delay flags.
findings.assessment: HPA autoscaling/v2 already represents ContainerResource metrics at the1.27 baseline; the converter preserves the raw-reviewed spec and changes the target. It does not set controller-manager command flags or parse kubectl HPA tables.

findings.change: Bound token metadata/cleanup, authorizer and admission-policy behavior change.
findings.assessment: Credentials are opaque kubeconfig tokens; the converter does not parse JWT claims or obtain automatic service-account token Secrets. Explicit versioned SSAR/LocalSAR checks and actual requests remain authoritative. VAP GA/default and match conditions can deny live dry runs; refusals occur before retirement. Selector-aware authorizers may deny broad Node/Pod listing to kubelet identities: grant the documented caller privileges, not node credentials. Authentication or authorization changes during a run still require failure reporting and explicit recovery.
residualScope: No older-server custom-authorizer or node-bound-token integration is claimed.

findings.change: PDB conditions, unhealthy eviction policy and scheduler preemption are corrected or graduated.
findings.assessment: The converter directly scales the DC and therefore separately checks synchronized observedGeneration and the entire affected source count against disruptionsAllowed. It does not invoke Eviction or rely on the scheduler enforcing PDBs during its own controller update. GA unhealthyPodEvictionPolicy does not grant permission to bypass the converter check; preemption patch fixes improve the cluster without altering this API contract.
residualScope: Unrelated concurrent preemption or unhealthy nodes can still reduce availability; no old-server scheduler-preemption test was run.

findings.change: OVN/SDN changes and Endpoints controller fixes affect actual traffic independently of resource acceptance.
findings.assessment: Policy selection checks already include optional ANP/BANP and unknown future pod-template-hash labels. Endpoint UID convergence and optional HTTP health checks are useful evidence but do not simulate OVN conntrack, all client protocols, secondary networks, egress-IP failover or large endpoint sets. SDN removal requires cluster network migration before DC conversion; the converter does not perform it.
requiredAction: Document protocol-specific application checks and the patch prerequisites in UDP-CONNTRACK; do not equate API Endpoints status with proof of all traffic paths.

findings.change: OVN endpoint replacement can leave stale UDP connections or external-gateway routes.
findings.assessment: The4.18.32 notes fix stale UDP conntrack for Service port!=targetPort after endpoint recreation.4.18.38 fixes external gateway routing to terminated Pods while a node is inactive. The migration replaces endpoint identities, so affected workloads need the applicable cluster fixes and protocol-specific checks. The notes alone do not establish the earliest affected patch.
requiredAction: Document4.18.32/4.18.38 fixes as conditional workload prerequisites; do not claim HTTP health tests cover UDP or external-gateway traffic.

findings.change: AzureFile in-tree implementation is removed while CSI translation remains; CSI runtime configuration and attachment behavior remain prerequisites.
findings.assessment: Upstream PR122576 changes AzureFile migration checks to unconditional true; this is not the same as Ceph/RBD becoming nonfunctional. Existing in-tree AzureFile-backed PVCs can continue through a functioning installed CSI driver. The converter reads bound PVC/PV references and PV node affinity, preserves volume settings and does not create/resize/delete production claims, alter drivers or clear finalizers. CSI attachment limits/mount success/SELinux relabeling are explicitly not simulated.
requiredAction: Document installed CSI/driver health, SELinux policy and volume attach limits as prerequisites; do not expand the unconditional removed-plugin denylist to AzureFile.

findings.change: CephFS and RBD volume types become nonfunctional, while SharedResourceCSI moves out of the base payload.
findings.assessment: CephFS/RBD inline sources, admission-added volumes, and PVC-backed PVs already trigger manual migration rather than unsafe automatic retirement. SharedResourceCSI is supported by the Builds1.1+ layered product after base-payload removal; it needs the installed layered driver, not a universal nonfunctional-plugin rejection.
residualScope: External data migration and layered CSI installation are operator actions; API preservation cannot restore an absent driver.

findings.change: PVC expansion-recovery statuses and PV reclaim/finalizer behavior change.
findings.assessment: Production reuses already-bound claims and does not resize them, create snapshots, delete PV/PVC pairs or remove storage finalizers. Administrators must perform the documented alpha RecoverVolumeExpansionFailure status cleanup where applicable. Qualification cleanup must respect reclaim policy and must not force-remove stuck production storage finalizers.
residualScope: A Bound claim alone does not prove successful attachment/relabel/mount.

findings.change: New4.18 installations use crun; upgrades from4.17 keep their prior runtime; runc shareProcessNamespace regression is patched.
findings.assessment: Runtime class/security/process-namespace intent is preserved and actual readiness is required. The4.18.30 note fixes runc startup with shareProcessNamespace=true. The4.18.34 note fixes systemd entrypoint ConfigMap permissions. These are kubelet/runtime environment defects rather than missing Deployment API fields.
requiredAction: Apply the applicable runtime fixes for workloads using shareProcessNamespace/systemd-mounted configuration; record runtime provenance when qualifying them.
residualScope: Release notes do not establish every affected starting patch; do not label all earlier patches broken.

findings.change: new-app builds, image import mode/pull tokens and registry-controller fixes affect fixtures and workload images.
findings.assessment: Production keeps BuildConfigs/ImageStreams and emits the supported image trigger annotation. The harness creates actual Docker/S2I builds and imports images and must retain a working registry, correct service-account ImagePullSecrets, matching CLI and trusted/reachable registries. Proxy defaults, rotation bugs and preserve-original manifest-list import affect build/pull outcomes, not the DC-to-Deployment resource version.
residualScope: Build success and a single architecture image do not qualify every S2I builder, image manifest type or registry topology.

findings.change: CLI streaming, output and authentication helpers evolve while fixture API contracts remain stable.
findings.assessment: Production does not shell out to oc. Fixture exec uses the -- command separator, not the removed legacy syntax; observations request JSON rather than parsing kubectl tables. Lease fixture explicitly uses coordination.k8s.io/v1 with resourceVersion compare-and-swap, not new coordinated LeaseCandidate election. WebSocket/SPDY proxy compatibility remains a fixture environment prerequisite.

findings.change: Operator-console, installer, host provisioning, monitoring and unrelated APIs are outside the migration operations.
findings.assessment: Changes scoped to CVO/OLM components, installers, VM/node creation, monitoring UIs, operator upgrades, topology displays and unrelated tools do not replace APIs called by the converter. Healthy infrastructure, current supported patches, functioning admission and application-specific runtime dependencies remain prerequisites. No compatibility claim is made for installing or upgrading these unrelated components.

findings.change: The reviewed upstream changelogs include security fixes affecting cluster health and node credentials.
findings.assessment: The converter does not invoke kubelet checkpoint, node logs/query, mutate Node owner references or provision Windows log permissions. Named CVEs therefore require cluster/operator remediation rather than converter wire-format changes. Use patched cluster payloads; upstream Kubernetes patch numbers alone do not identify OpenShift backport status.
residualScope: This is an impact review of named retrieved notes, not a claim that every CVE/advisory for every platform dependency is absent.

findings.change: Existing PV topology labels still constrain placement independently of PV nodeAffinity.
findings.assessment: At the reviewed0dcf787 source, checkScheduling reads PV nodeAffinity but does not evaluate legacy/beta topology labels used by the scheduler VolumeZone plugin. Removing PersistentVolumeLabel admission does not make existing volume-zone constraints disappear. Parent has separately reproduced the gap and owns a conservative refusal fix; this assessment does not claim to have run those reproductions.
requiredAction: Consolidated parent pass must guard or correctly evaluate existing PV beta/stable zone and region labels before source retirement, including old plans/admission-added PVCs as applicable.
Verify exact fixed source and tests before recording a compatibility assumption.

historicalSnapshots: Exact snapshots and source-bound resolution overlays require the external evidence bundle.
